exceptions.reason: The single source of the local-only Stripe webhook placeholder the end-to-end collection signs with. The value is not a credential: it is the local-e2e placeholder that docker-compose.yml also defaults to, and it is not accepted by Stripe in any real environment.

The Postman collections carry the same local-only placeholder so the webhook scenario can sign its payload. The production posture is unchanged: .env.prod.example keeps both PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET and SHOP_PAYMENT_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET commented out and marked ops-provisioned.
The local compose default for SHOP_PAYMENT_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET. It is a placeholder for the local stack only.
The generated Newman reports mirror the collection variables, so they repeat the same local-only placeholder. Any other secret value in these artifacts is still rejected by the scan.

The behavioural test of the live mode stripe guard needs a live mode key shape to prove the guard refuses it. The literal is a fabricated placeholder whose secret part is a run of the letter x, so it is not a credential and cannot authenticate against stripe.
The same fabricated placeholder for the restricted key form the guard must also refuse. The secret part is a run of the letter x.
The same fabricated placeholder for the test mode key that the guard must accept. The secret part is a run of the letter x, so it is not a credential.
